## RCA — root cause CONFIRMED at runtime (Phase 1 exit)

### Proven mechanism

Decorate-then-fit ordering. The marker is appended as the LAST characters of the
outbound body, and every comment fitter truncates from the RIGHT, so the marker is
always the first thing cut.

1. `outbound_comments.py:205` — `_decorate_outbound_comment` returns
   `f"{body}\n\n{RECONCILER_MARKER}"`; the marker is the tail of the string.
2. `adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py:516` — the ONE live Cloud comment send path:
   `body_arg = json.dumps(codec.to_wire(codec.fit_outbound(body)))`. `fit_outbound`
   receives the ALREADY-DECORATED body and truncates it.
3. `adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit` binary-searches the largest `text[:mid] + _ADF_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX`
   whose serialized ADF fits `_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT = 32000` — a right-truncation, so
   the trailing marker paragraph is discarded.

### Runtime evidence (not read from source — observed executing)

Driving a 40,000-char body through each real fitter (`.venv`, worktree `fix-illadopsis-marker`):

```
decorated len: 40032   ends with marker: True
A) current Cloud ADF send path -> fitted len 31887 | marker in fitted: False
                                | marker in RENDERED ADF: False
                                | tail: 'xxxx … [truncated by reconciler]'
B) rich=True ADF send path      -> marker in fitted: False
C) comment_limits.truncate_comment_body -> len 32767 | marker present: False
                                | tail: 'xxxx … [truncated by reconciler]'
D) DC WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound        -> len 32767 | marker present: False
```

All four fitters drop it. A short body keeps it, so the loss is length-triggered.

### The loop-breaker is provably inert (dynamic claim, observed)

Feeding the landed wire back through the inbound side
(`adf.adf_to_text` -> the `RECONCILER_MARKER in body_text` test at
`inbound_collection_diffs.py:148`):

```
short        -> inbound loop-breaker sees marker: True
over-length  -> inbound loop-breaker sees marker: False
```

So an over-length outbound echo is NOT recognised as ours on the next inbound pass —
exactly the loop the marker exists to break, disabled for precisely the comments most
likely to loop.

### The production signature matches experiment C exactly

The 836 marker-less duplicates (REB-1567 x418, REB-1931 x278, REB-2605 x140) are
**exactly 32767 chars ending in `" … [truncated by reconciler]"`** — byte-identical to
experiment C's `truncate_comment_body` output, i.e. the plaintext `_sanitize_comment`
send path that preceded the ADF-encode change (`27b868ba55`, 2026-08-13,
emersed-specific-mutt). That both dates the damage and confirms the mechanism is not
specific to today's fitter: it survived a send-path rewrite because the ORDERING, not
the fitter, is the defect.

### Defect legitimacy: `defect` (cited)

The behaviour violates an explicit, checked-in design invariant:

- `outbound_comments.py:72-78` — "marker token embedded in **every** outbound comment
  body ... Without the marker every outbound comment would re-appear inbound as a 'new
  Jira comment' and the bridge would loop."
- `_decorate_outbound_comment` docstring (`:198-204`) — "The marker survives ADF
  round-trip."
- Existing test `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_inbound_comments_diff.py:197`
  asserts `decorated.endswith(RECONCILER_MARKER)` and `:210` asserts the marker is in
  the emitted body — the contract is pinned, just never exercised over-length.

### Defect origin: UNATTRIBUTABLE (close class `preexisting`)

Date test applied. Both implicated sites blame (`git blame -w -C -M`) to
**`b534f47a7f` (2026-06-08) "Extract DSO ticket system + Jira reconciler into standalone
rebar"** — the repo's import commit (its parent `337ff71fdc` contains only `README.md`).
It carries no `rebar-ticket:` trailer.

The marker (`RECONCILER_MARKER`, DSO "Gap 1"/bug 85a1) and the comment truncation
(DSO bug 6afc-20ee-84e5-4dd5) arrived together in that single import, so there is no
later change that broke previously-working behaviour and no obligation-creating commit
inside this repo's history.

Searches that came up empty:
- `rebar show 6afc-20ee-84e5-4dd5` -> `ticket_not_found`; likewise `85a1`. `rebar search`
  returns only OTHER tickets that cite those DSO-era ids in prose, not the tickets.
- `git log -S'def truncate_comment_body'`, `-S'def _decorate_outbound_comment'`,
  `-S'RECONCILER_MARKER = "<!-- rebar:reconciler-echo -->"'` -> all bottom out at `b534f47a7f`.
- `git log --follow -- adapters/jira/comment_limits.py` -> same.

Divergence from the whole-file blame default: none to report — blame and the date test
agree, and both land on an untrailered pre-history import.

Explicitly NOT attributed to `27b868ba55` / emersed-specific-mutt: the 32767-char
production evidence predates it and proves the defect already existed.

## Debug report — fix pushed as Gerrit change 1983

### Proven root cause

Decorate-then-fit ordering. `_decorate_outbound_comment` (`outbound_comments.py:205`)
puts `RECONCILER_MARKER` at the very END of the body; every vendor fitter truncates
from the RIGHT. The one live Cloud comment send path
(`adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py:531`, `codec.to_wire(codec.fit_outbound(body))`)
received the already-decorated body, so the marker was always the first thing cut.

### Proof (runtime, discriminating)

- A 40,000-char decorated body fits to 31,887 chars ending in the truncation notice
  with NO marker; a short body keeps it -> the loss is length-triggered.
- All four fitters drop it (plain ADF, rich ADF, `truncate_comment_body`, DC wiki),
  which rules out "one bad fitter" and identifies the ORDERING as the defect.
- Feeding the landed wire back through the inbound predicate: short -> `True`,
  over-length -> `False`. The loop-breaker is provably inert.
- `truncate_comment_body` output is exactly 32767 chars ending in
  `" … [truncated by reconciler]"` — byte-identical to the 836 live duplicates,
  dating the damage to the pre-ADF-encode plaintext send path.

### The fix and its ordering rationale

`fit_preserving_marker(text, fit)` in `outbound_comments.py`, called from
`acli_cli_ops.add_comment`. It truncates the CONTENT and re-appends the decoration,
so the marker sits INSIDE the budget instead of hanging off its end — the reservation
the AC asked for, expressed as a re-ordering rather than as edits to four fitters.

Why here and not in the fitters: the fitters are shared with descriptions, which
carry no marker, and `jira_family` may not import `adapters/jira`. Making each
fitter marker-aware would have added a fourth copy of the marker literal and a
fourth of the truncation-notice literal. Instead the fitter is INJECTED as
`Callable[[str], str]`, so this backend-neutral core module still names no vendor
and no numeric limit (`test_backend_neutrality.py` passes), and the vendor's notice
is DERIVED from a single probe of `fit` rather than restated.

Behaviour: text not ending in the marker goes straight to `fit` (byte-identical —
verified); a decorated body already within the limit is returned untouched; an
over-limit one is rebuilt by binary-searching the largest content prefix whose
decorated form is a fixed point of `fit`.

Constraints checked: `_normalize_comment_body` still strips the marker, and the
dedup key is identical with and without it. Marker detection stays PRE-STRIP on the
rendered text — the inbound predicate now returns `True` for over-length echoes.

Robustness sweep: 70 combinations (5 body shapes x 7 lengths x rich/plain), zero
failures on all five postconditions plus idempotence.

### Would existing marker-less comments be re-posted? NO — verified, not assumed

The fix changes only what is POSTED; no comparison or dedup key changes. Running the
differ against a legacy marker-less landed body BEFORE and AFTER the fix gives an
identical result, so the change induces no re-post and needs no migration.

Separately: that body-equality path already misses for over-length comments today
(local key 32767 chars vs landed 31887) because the differ fits at
`_JIRA_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS` while the send path fits at the 32000 ADF limit. Filed as
`abusive-pebbly-sakimonkey` (e339-9709-15fe-419a). In production the ID-based primary
skip suppresses it.

### RED -> GREEN and mutation

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_outbound_comment_marker_survives_truncation.py`
— 5 tests at the observable send seam (the captured `--body` argument), including the
case that is over-limit only because the decoration pushed it over.

- RED first: 4 failed / 1 passed (the in-limit regression guard), each failing on the
  missing marker — the right reason.
- Held out: physically moved out of the tree before the implementation subagent ran;
  it never saw the file. GREEN on restore: 5 passed.
- Mutation 1 (re-introduce the exact root cause — restore `codec.fit_outbound(body)`):
  back to 4 failed. Mutation 2 (`notice = ""`): the truncation-notice test alone fails.
  The test has teeth on both axes.
- Refactoring litmus: assertions are on the emitted payload and decoded text only, no
  private names or source greps.

### Defect origin: UNATTRIBUTABLE (close class `preexisting`)

Date test applied. Both implicated sites blame (`-w -C -M`) to `b534f47a7f`
(2026-06-08), the DSO->rebar import commit whose parent holds only `README.md`. No
`rebar-ticket:` trailer. The marker (DSO bug 85a1) and the truncation (DSO bug 6afc)
arrived together, so no later change broke working behaviour. `rebar show` for both
DSO ids returns `ticket_not_found`; `git log -S` on all three symbols bottoms out at
the same import. Explicitly NOT charged to `27b868ba55` / emersed-specific-mutt: the
32767-char production evidence predates it.

### Scope, safety, siblings

- Caller sweep: `add_comment` has one enactment site
  (`dispatch_apply_phases.py:384`); no caller depends on the marker being absent or on
  the truncated length. Incidental only.
- Restoration, not creation: no new entry point, no new dependency, no test weakened.
- Construct sweep: no other trailing token is appended after content and then fitted.
- Parity census — CLI: N/A. MCP/API: N/A. Library facade: N/A. Automated callers: both
  producers (`_diff_comments`, `_map_comments_for_create`) funnel through the one fixed
  site. Dual-direction: inbound has no fit. Backends: Cloud fixed; DC applies NO fit on
  the comment send path at all, so it cannot drop the marker — but its `sanitize_comment`
  has no production caller, filed as `community-sediment-snipe` (b9b4-f460-2d54-4872).

### Gates

`make lint` green (ratchet `active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`); `make typecheck`
`Success: no issues found in 613 source files`; full unit sweep **11942 passed, 44
skipped, 0 failures** (includes the repo-wide oracles).

### Replication

Through the real entry point with the report's own shape (40,000-char body): `--body`
32,000 chars (<= 32767), marker present, truncation notice present, inbound
loop-breaker recognises it. The original report no longer reproduces. No live Jira was
touched at any point — all fixture/stub.

## Gerrit 1983 patchset 2 — addressed an LLM-Review -1 (tests only)

**Finding (valid):** `fit_preserving_marker`'s undecorated fast path
(`outbound_comments.py:256`, `if not text.endswith(RECONCILER_MARKER): return fit(text)`)
was untested, even though the change explicitly contracted it as "descriptions and
undecorated bodies stay byte-identical". A guarantee asserted in prose and not pinned.
That branch carries every non-comment caller, so its blast radius is wider than the
marker path that WAS tested.

**Fix:** `fit_preserving_marker` is now driven directly against the real `AdfCodec`
fitter over 8 shapes — empty, short, multiline, a marker-lookalike ending in `-->`,
trailing-newline and trailing-space bodies, and two OVER-limit bodies — each asserting
byte-identity with a bare `fit(text)`. A companion test proves the over-limit case
genuinely truncates, so the two sides are not trivially agreeing by returning the input.

**Mutation check — the first version had no teeth, and the check caught it.** The
suggested mutation (`rstrip()` on the fast path) initially SURVIVED: none of my inputs
had trailing whitespace left after fitting (the over-limit ones end in the truncation
notice, the rest in prose), so `rstrip` was a no-op on every case. That is precisely the
tautology a mutation check exists to expose. The `trailing_whitespace` and
`trailing_spaces` cases were added to close it. Three mutations now all return RED:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| A — fast path `.rstrip()` | 2 failed |
| B — fast path decorates undecorated text | 9 failed |
| C — fast path removed entirely | 3 failed |

**Gates on patchset 2:** ruff clean; complexity ratchet `active=49 new=0 increased=0
stale=0`; mypy `613 source files` clean; full unit suite **11951 passed, 44 skipped, 0
failed**. No production code changed from patchset 1 — tests only. Amended onto the same
`Change-Id` (`I2d6d36f…`), so this is patchset 2, not a duplicate change. No `recheck`
was issued: `Verified` was already +1, so this was a review finding, not a CI fault.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

`_decorate_outbound_comment` (`outbound_comments.py`) appends `RECONCILER_MARKER` AFTER the comment body. The outbound comment-limit truncation (`adapters/jira/comment_limits.py`, `_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX = \" … [truncated by reconciler]\"`) then cuts the composed text at the 32767-char limit, which removes the trailing marker paragraph.

## Impact

A comment whose body exceeds the limit lands in Jira with NO marker. That comment is then:
- unrecognisable as the reconciler's own echo on the inbound side (the loop-breaker at `inbound_collection_diffs.py` tests for the marker in the body text), and
- unrecognisable to any tooling that identifies bot-authored comments by the marker.

## Evidence (live)

Found during the duplicate-comment cleanup (`darkish-enormous-raptors` / `76b2-4b5f-5682-45e5`). 836 Jira comments across REB-1567 (418), REB-1931 (278) and REB-2605 (140) are marker-less. Each is authored by the bridge bot accountId `712020:6471376f-4e5e-4ed2-8c05-330827bc387e`, is exactly 32767 rendered chars, ends in `_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX`, and repeats ~139 times identically. They had to be excluded from the marker-based cleanup as non-candidates.

## Expected vs Actual

- Expected: every outbound comment carries the marker regardless of body length.
- Actual: any comment over the limit loses it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Outbound truncation reserves room for the marker — truncate the BODY to (limit - len(marker) - len(suffix)) and append the marker after truncating, so the composed text is <= the limit AND ends with the marker.
- [x] Unit test: a body longer than the limit produces an outbound payload that is <= the limit and whose rendered text contains RECONCILER_MARKER. RED on current code.
- [x] Unit test: the truncation suffix is still present on a truncated body (the existing truncation contract is not broken).

file_impact.reason: Add fit_preserving_marker: a vendor-neutral marker-preserving wrapper around any comment fitter, beside RECONCILER_MARKER and _decorate_outbound_comment.
The one live Cloud comment send path; route codec.fit_outbound through fit_preserving_marker so the marker survives truncation.
RED->GREEN oracle: an over-length comment must round-trip with the marker intact and the truncation suffix retained.

compiled_state.title: Outbound comment truncation drops the RECONCILER_MARKER, defeating the loop-breaker for >32767-char comments
